Former Italian Prime Minister Mario Draghi said young people feel “no one is listening to them,” linking recent youth riots in Paris, Milan and other European cities to frustration about their future.
Speaking to Bloomberg, the former European Central Bank chief called it “a case of blocked expectations.” 
He said that for the young, social justice means fairness between generations, which is hard to maintain without economic growth. 
He said many feel they can’t easily find a job. 
He added that they see society changing fast through technology and “feel unequipped to deal with that.”

BIG: Websites around the world were taken offline after two critical security flaws were found in PHP, a programming language that powers much of the internet. 
A fix was released on Wednesday afternoon. 
Cybersecurity agencies urged organizations that couldn’t update in time to take their sites down. 
Finland shut down its government’s public web services, and Dutch agencies and the lower house of parliament also went offline. 
Wikimedia took some systems down, cutting access to parts of Wikipedia. 
The flaws were found with the help of AI, through an OpenAI program called Patch the Planet. 
Security firm Wiz called them the “most severe vulnerabilities ever discovered” by AI. 
The bugs had gone undetected for more than a decade. 
Details leaked on social media on Tuesday, forcing an early announcement. 
The White House called the discovery “American innovation strengthening our national security.”
